chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ubayd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Dahqan from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tatari from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, the seller of al-Sabiri, from Ajlan, Abu Salih, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) killed forty with his own hand on the Day of Hunayn.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq or Imam Ali depending on context, here referring to the speaker)

ai.seo_question: How many people did Imam Ali kill with his own hand during the Battle of Hunayn?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the exceptional martial prowess of Imam Ali (as) during the Battle of Hunayn, where he personally slew forty enemies, a feat often cited in Shia scholarship to demonstrate his unique status among the companions. While the Battle of Hunayn is primarily associated with the Prophet Muhammad (saw), this specific account underscores Ali's (as) active combat role and physical strength in the early Islamic conflicts. The emphasis on 'with his own hand' serves to authenticate the report and elevate the spiritual and physical merit of the Imam in the eyes of the faithful.
